summary.text: A 2.5-year-old male castrated Rhodesian Ridgeback was presented to the Vetsuisse Faculty with an apparently rapidly growing pigmented, raised iris mass. The left eye had a rapidly growing iridal mass; the right eye had a pigmented lesion since puppyhood. Ocular ultrasound of the left eye showed the iridocorneal angle and ciliary body unaffected, and preoperative diagnostics were declined for the right eye.

Therapeutic TCIP was given before surgery, three sessions in the left eye and four in the right eye, with regrowth recorded after each session and tumor progression and corneal opacity illustrated after therapy. Histopathology gave iris melanocytoma in the left eye and melanocytic proliferation (hyperplasia or melanocytoma) in the right eye.

Under general anesthesia each eye had TCIP delineation of the incision lines followed by sector iridectomy, at 6 months for the left eye and 8 months for the right. Moderate intraocular hemorrhage, hyphema, fibrin, anterior uveitis and posterior synechiae occurred; topical and systemic NSAID and antibiotic therapy was given after surgery.

At last follow-up, 11 months for the left eye and 9 months for the right, both eyes were visual and comfortable with no regrowth, and each had posterior synechiae, corneal deposits, dyscoria and photophobia. Owners reported photophobia persisting to the last follow-up.

summary.text: A 6.5-year-old male castrated German Shepherd was presented to the Vetsuisse Faculty with an apparently rapidly growing pigmented, raised iris mass. History included chronic superficial keratitis in both eyes. Preoperative high-resolution and ocular ultrasound showed the iridocorneal angle, and for ocular ultrasound the ciliary body, unaffected.

One session of therapeutic TCIP, given 3 months after presentation, and tacrolimus eye drops twice per day preceded surgery, and regrowth was recorded after the TCIP session. Histopathology gave iris melanocytoma; figure captions illustrate tumor progression and corneal opacity after therapeutic TCIP.

Delineation TCIP and sector iridectomy under general anesthesia were done at the Table 1 timeline of 8 months, with moderate intraocular hemorrhage, hyphema, fibrin, anterior uveitis and posterior synechiae. Intracameral tPA was injected 2 weeks post op, with topical steroid, antibiotic, mydriatic and lubricant and systemic steroid and analgesic therapy.

At the last follow-up, 14 months, the eye was visual and comfortable with no regrowth, with posterior synechiae, dyscoria, subepithelial corneal lipid deposits and photophobia. The text and Table 1 disagree on whether the eye was the right or the left.

summary.text: A 6.5-year-old male intact Labrador Retriever was presented to the Vetsuisse Faculty with an apparently rapidly growing pigmented, raised iris mass, with progressive increase in iridal pigment in the left eye. Gonioscopy and high-resolution ultrasound showed the iridocorneal angle unaffected, and no therapy was given before sector iridectomy.
Histopathology of the excised left-eye mass gave iris melanocytoma, with no mitotic figures found in 10 high-power fields and tumor-free margins reported for the series.

One month after presentation the eye had TCIP delineation of the incision lines and sector iridectomy under general anesthesia, with moderate intraocular hemorrhage from the second iris cut, then intracameral tPA 6 days post op and topical NSAID, antibiotic, mydriatic and lubricant plus systemic steroid and antibiotic. Focal anterior lens capsular fibrosis was noted.
At the last follow-up, 5 months, the left eye was visual and comfortable with no regrowth, with posterior synechiae and dyscoria; normal IOP was maintained.

summary.text: A 2-year-old male castrated Scottish Fold cat was presented to the Vetsuisse Faculty with an apparently rapidly growing pigmented, raised iris mass and rapidly increasing iridal pigment in the left eye. Preoperative diagnostics were declined and no therapy was given before sector iridectomy; the Schirmer Tear Test was omitted.
Histopathology gave diffuse iris melanoma in the left eye, with no mitotic figures found in 10 high-power fields and a photomicrograph showing the surgical margin beyond normal appearing tissue.

Six weeks after presentation, therapeutic TCIP of flat pigmented lesions, TCIP delineation around the raised tumor and sector iridectomy were done under general anesthesia, with moderate intraocular hemorrhage and the pupillary margin retained. Topical NSAID, antibiotic, mydriatic, lubricant and systemic NSAID and antibiotic therapy followed. Enucleation was discussed and declined.

At the last follow-up, 12 months, the eye was visual and comfortable with no regrowth and dyscoria; photophobia was not observed. The Figure 2 caption reports no grossly evident regrowth 1 year postoperatively.
